sub_areas.name: Bolton
sub_areas.note: Southeast Caledon beside the Humber River, the town's most populous community (2021 population 26,795) and its primary administrative and commercial centre (Wikipedia). OGS point query at the Wikipedia coordinate (43.8972, -79.7381) returns clay-to-silt till (unit 5d) over Georgian Bay Formation; a second point on the Humber valley floor (43.8833, -79.7333) returns modern alluvium (unit 19) over Georgian Bay Formation.

sub_areas.name: Caledon East
sub_areas.note: Central Caledon, seat of Town Hall at 6311 Old Church Road (Town deck checklist letterhead); population 5,575 (Wikipedia). OGS point query at the Wikipedia coordinate (43.8697, -79.8667) returns glaciofluvial river/delta deposits (unit 7) over Queenston Formation, the same result as the reference coordinate.

sub_areas.name: Caledon Village
sub_areas.note: Northwest Caledon on the Escarpment upland; population 1,909 (Wikipedia). OGS point query at the Wikipedia coordinate (43.8604, -79.9958) returns stone-poor sandy silt till (unit 5b) over Amabel Formation dolostone (Silurian).

sub_areas.name: Inglewood
sub_areas.note: Village on the Credit River in west-central Caledon; population 1,175 (Wikipedia). OGS point query at the Wikidata coordinate (43.7956, -79.9339) returns clay-to-silt till (unit 5d) over Queenston Formation.

sub_areas.name: Palgrave
sub_areas.note: Compact Rural Community about 10 km north of Bolton (Wikipedia). OGS point query at the Wikipedia coordinate (43.9486, -79.8339) returns ice-contact stratified sand and gravel (unit 6) over Georgian Bay Formation; the Town deck checklist flags Oak Ridges Moraine site-plan control as an applicable-law item for this part of Caledon, though the OGS layer does not carry the moraine name.

sub_areas.name: Alton
sub_areas.note: Village in northwest Caledon, established 1820; population 1,116 (Wikipedia). OGS point query at the Wikipedia coordinate (43.8603, -80.0686) returns glaciofluvial deposits (unit 7) over thin Silurian units mapped together as Whirlpool/Manitoulin/Cabot Head/Fossil Hill (shale-, sandstone- or dolostone-dominated).

sub_areas.name: Cheltenham
sub_areas.note: Small village in southwest Caledon, population 729 (Wikipedia). OGS point query at the Wikidata coordinate (43.7516, -79.9230) returns fine-textured glaciolacustrine silt and clay (unit 8a) over Queenston Formation; the Cheltenham Badlands (exposed Queenston shale) lie nearby but were not point-queried.

sub_areas.name: Belfountain
sub_areas.note: Hamlet on the Credit River below the Escarpment (Wikipedia). OGS point query at the Wikipedia coordinate (43.7942, -80.0142) returns glaciofluvial deposits (unit 7) over the thin Silurian Whirlpool/Manitoulin/Cabot Head/Fossil Hill units.

sub_areas.name: Mayfield West
sub_areas.note: Suburban growth area on the Brampton border along Mayfield Road (Wikipedia coordinate 43.7564, -79.8292). OGS point query returns clay-to-silt till (unit 5d) over Queenston Formation, the same till the OGS maps across south Peel.

bedrock.formation: Queenston Formation (central and south Caledon), Georgian Bay Formation (east: Bolton, Palgrave), Amabel Formation dolostone (Escarpment cap at Caledon Village), and thin Silurian Whirlpool/Manitoulin/Cabot Head/Fossil Hill units on the Escarpment slope (Alton, Belfountain); all per OGS MRD219 point queries.
bedrock.description: Queenston: red shale and siltstone, minor green shale and siltstone, and variable calcareous siltstone to sandstone and limestone interbeds (Ordovician). Georgian Bay: interbedded grey-green to dark grey shale and fossiliferous calcareous siltstone to bioclastic limestone (Ordovician). Amabel: white to blue-grey, thick- to massive-bedded dolostone (Silurian). Whirlpool/Manitoulin/Cabot Head/Fossil Hill: thin units variously shale-, sandstone-, dolostone- or limestone-dominated (Silurian). Queenston returned at the reference coordinate, Caledon East, Inglewood, Cheltenham and Mayfield West; Georgian Bay at both Bolton points and Palgrave; Amabel at Caledon Village; the thin Silurian group at Alton and Belfountain.
bedrock.depth_note: Depth to bedrock was not retrieved (no drift-thickness dataset queried). No OGS surficial query point in Caledon returned unit 3 (bedrock at or near surface); every point returned till, glaciofluvial, glaciolacustrine, ice-contact or alluvial cover of unstated thickness. Bedrock exposure is known at the Cheltenham Badlands and the Forks of the Credit from general references but was not verified by point query here.

implications_for_piles: The Town of Caledon's Building Inspections page lists 'helical anchors' by name in its footing/structural-slab inspection ('Footing or structural slab (foundations, piers, posts, sonotubes, helical anchors, rebar)'), so a pile-founded deck is inspected at the same stage as a poured pier, before any concrete or backfill.

The Town's 2015 deck checklist requires detailed construction drawings to include 'approval documents such as CCMC or BMEC and Minister's Rulings', which is the route a proprietary helical pile system is documented under; the Aug-2024 checklist asks for concrete pier diameter, spacing and depth on the foundation plan and section, so a helical design substitutes engineer-stamped pile information for those items.

The conventional baseline the Town's hosted standard details set for a wood deck is a poured concrete pier 'MIN. 1200mm BELOW GRADE ON UNDISTURBED SOIL', with the soil bearing capacity to be determined before construction; that is the depth and bearing question a helical pile design answers by torque and engineer review rather than by excavation.

Soil texture changes sharply across Caledon: OGS maps sand-and-gravel outwash (unit 7) at Caledon East, Alton and Belfountain, ice-contact sand and gravel (unit 6) at Palgrave, clay-to-silt till (unit 5d) at Bolton, Inglewood and Mayfield West, silt and clay (unit 8a) at Cheltenham, and sandy till over Amabel dolostone (unit 5b) at Caledon Village; pile depth and capacity therefore cannot be transferred between villages, and near-surface dolostone or shale on the Escarpment is a refusal condition to check before installation.

The Town deck checklists flag Niagara Escarpment Commission, Credit Valley Conservation, Toronto and Region Conservation and Oak Ridges Moraine site-plan approvals as applicable-law items 'if applicable'; those agency clearances precede the building permit in the affected parts of Caledon. No site-specific depth, torque or capacity figures were retrieved.

permits.authority: Town of Caledon Building Services (letterhead on the Town's deck checklist: 'Building Services, 6311 Old Church Road, Caledon, ON L7C 1J6, 905-584-2272'); the Town's web pages also say 'Building division' and 'building department'
permits.deck_permit_required_when: The Town's Building Permits page lists 'decks (only if the deck is higher than 24" off the ground at any point)' under projects that require a permit, and 'A deck with a finished level of not more than 60 cm (24") above finished grade at any point' under projects that do not. No area threshold is stated for decks; any accessory structure attached to an existing structure is treated as an addition requiring a permit. Zoning clearance is required before any project starts.
permits.footing_depth_requirement: The Town's deck checklists ask for a foundation plan with 'diameter of concrete pier locations and spacing' and a section showing 'location, depth of concrete piers' (Aug 2024), and refer applicants to the TACBOC/LMCBO standard details the Town hosts, whose wood-deck sheet prints 'POURED CONCRETE PIER MIN. 1200mm BELOW GRADE ON UNDISTURBED SOIL' and note 7 'CONCRETE PIERS SHALL BEAR ON UNDISTURBED SOIL. THE BEARING CAPACITY OF THE SOIL SHALL BE DETERMINED PRIOR TO CONSTRUCTION.' Helical piles: the 2015 deck checklist requires 'approval documents such as CCMC or BMEC and Minister's Rulings' with the construction drawings; the inspections page names 'helical anchors' in the footing inspection. No Caledon-specific helical depth or engineer wording beyond that was found.
inspections: Footing or structural slab (foundations, piers, posts, sonotubes, helical anchors, rebar) - excavation complete, before any concrete is poured; engineer's site report if on fill
Plumbing final and HVAC final (prior to occupancy, where applicable)
Building final (occupancy) - all construction complete including exterior work and grading; ESA final certificate provided
permits.fee_note: 2026 Fees By-law (By-law 2025-105, Schedule B building fees): '(j) Decks, porches, basement walkout, etc. to detached, semis, townhouses, duplexes - Each - $192.00'; the same schedule states 'The minimum permit fee shall be $193.00'. A non-refundable minimum fee is collected at application; if not paid within ten business days a full resubmission is required.
permits.timeline_note: Town states that once a complete application is paid, Ontario Building Code review timeframes apply: 'Residential Dwelling, Tents, Demountable Stages or Demountable Support Structures - 10 business days; Small Buildings and Additional Residential Units - 15 business days'. Which class a deck falls in is not stated on the page. Resubmissions have no guaranteed review time and 'could add two or more weeks'. Inspections: book with 24 hours notice before 1 p.m. for next-day service; inspections run Monday to Friday 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
permits.portal_note: All building permit applications are accepted online only, in PDF, through the Town's Building Services web form (forms.caledon.ca, 'BuildingServicesForm'); the linked Building Permits page is the public entry point and hosts the 'Construction Companion' smart permit guide, checklists and the 2026 Fees By-law.

climate.station: Orangeville MOE (Climate ID 6155790; 43.92 N, 80.09 W; 411.5 m), about 19 km WNW of the reference coordinate, on the same Escarpment upland as Caledon Village and Alton; Toronto Pearson (Climate ID 6158731, 173.4 m, about 28 km SE) used as the low-elevation comparison for Bolton and Mayfield West
climate.normals_period: 1981-2010 for Orangeville MOE (temperature computed from 1981-2006, 26 years, code C; frost-free from 18 years, code D); 1991-2020 for Toronto Pearson
climate.freeze_thaw_note: Orangeville MOE 1981-2010: January daily minimum -11.6 C; 76.8 days/yr with daily maximum <= 0 C; 170.6 days/yr with daily minimum <= 0 C, so roughly 94 days a year cross 0 C between night and day (derived by subtraction); last spring frost May 20, first fall frost Sept 30; 151.5 cm annual snowfall. Toronto Pearson 1991-2020 for the low-lying southeast (Bolton, Mayfield West): January mean -5.0 C, January minimum -8.9 C, 34.2 days/yr below -10 C, 49.5 days/yr max <= 0 C, 130.6 days/yr min <= 0 C, 174 frost-free days (Apr 27 - Oct 20), 114.5 cm snowfall. Caledon spans about 200 m of relief, so the true figure for a given site lies between these two stations.
